items.title: RealPRO Select helps lift Realtor.com revenue
items.description: Move , the parent company of Realtor.com , said the momentum generated by RealPRO Select in fiscal year 2026 has carried over into the first quarter of fiscal year 2027. During the first quarter of FY 2027, Realtor.com recorded $160 million in revenue, up 5% year over year, marking the segment’s eighth consecutive quarter of growth. These financial results were highlighted during News Corp ’s fiscal year 2026 fourth-quarter earnings call on Wednesday evening. “In a housing market constrained by 7%-plus mortgage rates , Damian [Eales] and the team have exhibited exceptional discipline in their operational focus and AI integration, and that approach has converted revenue growth into meaningful bottom-line expansion,” Robert Thomson, the CEO of News Corp, said during the earnings call. RealPRO Select grows News Corp executives attributed Realtor.com ’s strong revenue performance to the growth of RealPRO Select. The company said it is focused on enhancing the platform with stronger lead generation, branding, productivity tools and training capabilities. Realtor.com also focused on the expansion of RealAssist AI during Q1, including the launch of a pilot of RealAssist in Rich Communication Services (RCS), integrated directly into Google search and available on iOS and Android. “The pilot is already attracting new users, driving strong engagement, and helping us capture pre-search intent earlier in the buyer journey before consumers ever enter a browser,” Damian Eales, the CEO of Move, wrote in a blog post about the company's quarterly performance. In addition, Realtor.com also launched RealAssist AI for Realtor.com+, which Eales said helps agents onboard their clients faster, build more tailored searches, summarize client activity and draft follow-ups in their own voice. “The platform is already supporting thousands of successful agent-client connections, and early feedback on these AI tools has been very positive,” Eales wrote. Other highlights Eales also highlighted the relaunch of the My Home dashboard, which now includes a collaboration with Opendoor . Eales said this is encouraging sellers to engage a listing agent much earlier in their journey. In addition, News Corp also noted that Comscore data shows 4.9 visits per unique user to Realtor.com, up 8% annually, and an average of 263 million monthly visits in the quarter, which the company said represents a “substantial” lead over Redfin and Homes.com . Despite these strong numbers, Realtor.com noted that lead volume was down 11%, which the portal attributed to broader market conditions and its repositioning of customer acquisitions to higher-quality and higher-value leads. “Despite a constrained housing market , Realtor.com’s strategy is delivering positive results, and we’re well positioned to grow as conditions improve,” Eales wrote. “Our focus remains on investing in our audience and AI tools that enhance a consumer’s experience and augment the role of the professional agent.” Overall, News Corp’s digital real estate services segment generated $529 million in revenue, up 10% from a year prior. The company as a whole generated $2.28 billion in revenue, a 6% annual increase, and net income of $215 million, up 43% compared to a year prior. Related More: Earnings News Corp. Realtor.com

items.title: American Housing Corp names leadership for new Austin division
items.description: The American Housing Corporation launched an Austin homebuilding division and named three industry veterans to lead the new operation as it ramps up an infill-focused, prefabricated rowhome platform, the company announced this week. Austin is the launch market for the company’s infill homebuilding strategy, which centers on designing, manufacturing and constructing urban rowhomes. The move comes as builders look for ways to add “missing middle” housing in supply-constrained, high-cost markets without relying solely on traditional greenfield development. Parker Scott, a former division president at LGI Homes , was appointed general manager, Daniel Green will serve as director of construction operations and Luke Allen will serve as director of land. Scott brings more than 20 years of homebuilding sales and operational experience to the role. Green joins from senior construction positions at Homebound , ATCO Structures and Perry Homes , where he focused on building operations and execution systems. Allen, who previously held land roles at Lennar and Ashton Woods , will oversee land acquisition, underwriting and pipeline development for the Austin market. In October 2026, American Housing Corp completed its “Demo 2” prototype using a componentized, prefabricated building system. The company is building a 250,000-square-foot manufacturing plant in Southeast Austin designed to produce up to 1,200 homes annually, according to the announcement. The factory-scale approach is intended to standardize production, shorten build times and provide more cost certainty, which could appeal to capital providers and municipalities looking for scalable infill housing solutions. For real estate investors and lenders, the combination of an infill land strategy with a controlled-offsite construction environment could change underwriting assumptions around cycle times and construction risk. Alongside the Austin division launch, the company restructured its real estate operations and parted ways with co-founder Bobby Fijan. The firm credited Fijan with helping establish its early real estate footprint and championing urban, family-sized housing. Related More: homebuilder Texas

items.description: Onity's 50%+ recapture rate raises the bar for servicers By Colin McNamara Published November 05, 2026, 4:24 p.m. EST 2 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email What's at Stake: Whether smaller lenders can maintain volume as the market enters a difficult 2027. Supporting Data: After spending last quarter in the red, Onity recorded $3.5 million in net income attributable to common shareholders and $29.6 million in adjusted pretax income. Overview bullets generated by AI with editorial review. Onity Group's recapture rate topped 50% in the third quarter, up 18 percentage points from a year ago. The lender is using its servicing book to grow volume while the rest of the industry shrinks. The servicing segment produced $7 million in pretax income and $29 million on an adjusted basis, up from $12 million in the second quarter. Originations totaled $23.7 million in adjusted pretax income, down 15% from $27.8 million the previous quarter, according to the company's third quarter earnings release. Processing Content "The big benefit for them is being a relatively large servicer," Bose George, mortgage finance analyst at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, told National Mortgage News. "In the higher-for-longer rate environment , they are somewhat better positioned being a big servicer with a smaller origination footprint." A model for smaller lenders Onity's performance signals a shift some lenders can make. While it's difficult for larger originators to outperform the market due to their scale, George said, smaller lenders should take a more servicing-forward approach to maintain volume as the market enters what is expected to be a difficult year in 2027. Glen Messina, chairman, president and CEO at Onity "In a market environment that is increasingly favorable for servicing and more challenging for originations, our complementary businesses returned the company to profitability and more than doubled adjusted return on equity from the prior quarter," Onity President and CEO Glen Messina said in a press release Thursday. Growing the servicing book Onity reported $24.7 billion in total servicing additions last quarter, bringing its total unpaid balance to $343 billion, up 9% from the same quarter last year. Subservicing additions reached $53 billion by the end of the quarter, exceeding its full-year target. Chief Financial Officer Sean O'Neil said on the earnings call that Onity plans to be more selective in its expansion going forward. Cost advantage The company has been pursuing efficiencies by reducing its headcount and improving technology. It did not disclose layoffs on the call, but said its investments have decreased the cost per loan to $94, below the independent mortgage bank average of $112 per loan. "The technology, not just for them but the whole industry, has really improved," George said. "The expectation is that costs will continue to come down as technology becomes more efficient." Earnings turnaround After spending last quarter in the red, Onity recorded $3.5 million in net income attributable to common shareholders and $29.6 million in adjusted pretax income. Both came in below last year's marks but were notable improvements over its second-quarter performance, which featured a $12.9 million net loss. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.93, beating BTIG's prediction of $1.60 and S&P Capital IQ's consensus estimate of $1.67. Revenue totaled $278.1 million, down slightly from $282.9 million in the second quarter and $280.3 million last year. Colin McNamara Reporter Colin McNamara is a reporter for National Mortgage News. items.title: Bobby Flay and Brooke Williamson Reveal What It’s Like To Have 2 Celebrity Chefs in a Home Kitchen—and How They’re Prepping for Thanksgiving
items.description: Food Network chefs Bobby Flay and Brooke Williamson are getting ready for another Thanksgiving celebration at their beautiful Hamptons home, and they've shared their best tips and tricks ahead of the holiday. In an interview with People magazine, the power couple said that their best advice is to start dinner prep early. “Prep as much as you can ahead of time,” said Williamson, 48. “I think stuffing tastes better the next day, once it’s had a chance to meld together.” Flay , 61, dropped another helpful piece of advice: “Have chicken stock on your stove. It reheats the sliced turkey, which ultimately gets dried out no matter what you do. It can also thin out gravy that gets too thick.” While one might assume that having two celebrity chefs in a household can feel like a case of too many cooks in the kitchen, the duo said it’s never a problem for them. Loading... Celebrity chefs Bobby Flay and Brooke Williamson are preparing to host a Tuscan-inspired Thanksgiving dinner. Winnie Au/PEOPLE Loading... The couple shared a look at the home kitchen of their New York City residence with People magazine. Winnie Au/PEOPLE Loading... Despite each having command of the kitchen, they say "it never feels like we're in each other's way." Winnie Au/PEOPLE “We definitely split up the work,” said Williamson. “It never feels like we’re in each other’s way. It feels like it makes sense.” Flay and Williamson invited the publication into the kitchen of their New York City home, showing off the gorgeous cabinets and generously sized island. After a recent trip to Italy , the couple told the magazine that they’re planning a Tuscan-inspired feast this year, joking that it’ll be a “mini ‘Brady Bunch’” scenario with their blended families. Flay is dad to 30-year-old Sophie , while Williamson has a son, Hudson , 18. In September, Flay spoke about the home kitchens he has in his two residences—his Tribeca pad and an estate in the Hamptons. “The kitchen is spacious, and I make three meals a day in there,” he told The Wall Street Journal . ”The space relaxes me and allows me to cook for family and friends.” In his home out East, the kitchen is not just a place to whip up delicious meals. The room functions more like a full-fledged restaurant. “On the other side of my sizable island are three French cafe tables for guests,” he explained. The setup is even equipped with a professional fryer, which he described as a “recent kitchen splurge.” Among his latest kitchen tools is a utensil he’s relied on for years: “I still have the chef’s knife I used at [the French Culinary Institute],” he shared. “When [I] prepare food with it, the feel reminds me that I’m still learning every day." The kitchen of the Amagansett home is his favorite place to cook and where he has typically hosted Thanksgiving. Loading... Flay recently gifted Williamson a gorgeous diamond ring to show his commitment without entering another marriage. Winnie Au/PEOPLE Flay built the dwelling from the ground up during his marriage to “Law and Order: SVU” actress Stephanie March . The former couple, who divorced in 2015, hosted a turkey dinner for a staggering 50 guests at their first Thanksgiving in the home. “I prepared two 30-pound turkeys and cooked sides for days,” he recalled in a 2013 interview with Elle Decor . “I stand at my kitchen island from the minute I get out here to the minute I leave.” Although Flay has publicly discussed his desire to steer clear of matrimony after three divorces, he and Williamson have agreed on an alternative way to show their commitment to each other. “She’s like, ‘I just want a big ring and a big party,’ and I was like, ‘I love that idea because my marriages have not lasted, unfortunately,’” he told People. Explaining that the “most important thing” is to “make sure that Brooke feels like she’s committed to,” he recalled of the moment he gifted her a “giant diamond ring” during a trip to London. Williamson describes the flashy piece of jewelry as “the perfect ring,” adding that “it’s very sparkly.” Although she was initially thrown off by the gesture, she now sports the rock on her right hand. “I thought it was incredibly thoughtful,” said Williamson. “He said just because I don’t feel the need to get married or want to get married again doesn’t mean that you don’t deserve the big, beautiful ring that comes along with it.” While Flay has been private about his past relationships, he admits he’s been more open this time around, and cites all they have in common for his “confidence” about their partnership. “I feel very confident about this,” he said of the pair’s connection. “There’s so many wonderful things about it.” Get real estate news in your inbox Sign up now Hannah Chambers is a senior celebrity and lifestyle reporter who joined Realtor.com in 2026. She has been writing entertainment and lifestyle content since 2016, with her work appearing in Cosmopolitan, BravoTV, NYLON, Bustle, Elite Daily, and The Zoe Report, among other publications. Hannah received a bachelor’s degree in journalism from The University of Maine. In her spare time, she loves to chat about pop culture and is a major fan of reality TV.

items.title: Mortgage rates fell and demand steadied as inventory dipped
items.description: Mortgage rates fell, demand stabilized and inventory had a noticeable decline last week. But are the changes in demand and inventory data about seasonality, or has the housing market changed with the recent mortgage rate decline? Let’s take a look at the weekend tracker and see what the data is telling us with rates falling the last three weeks. 10-year yield and mortgage rates In the 2026 HousingWire forecast , I anticipated the following ranges: Mortgage rates between 5.75% and 6.75% The 10-year yield fluctuating between 3.80% and 4.60% What a crazy time in the bond market recently: the key level of 5.35% has not only held since early October, but the reversal has been truly nice to watch. The midterm elections , which changed the control of the House and Senate, have added another variable into the mortgage rate equation. I discussed what Congress can do to help lower mortgage rates on this episode of the HousingWire Daily podcast with Editor in Chief Sarah Wheeler, but for now the head-and-shoulders pattern of the 10-year yield is still somewhat intact, though a fight for it to break lower is happening. I wouldn’t get too excited about mortgage rates until the 10-year yield can break under 4.70% and have follow-through bond buying, but mortgage rates have fallen and demand has stabilized over the last few weeks. Mortgage spreads Mortgage spreads have worsened recently, but they’re still trending near multiyear lows. Traditionally, when mortgage rates escalate with the 10-year yield and then make a big reversal — like we just had from a 5.35% 10-year yield top that dropped down toward 4.82% — spreads do get worse to try to compress mortgage rate volatility. That said, if mortgage spreads weren’t near multiyear lows right now, we'd have no chance of getting mortgage rates below 7.25%, and demand wouldn't have stabilized recently. Now that spreads have moved up from this year's lows, we can clearly see that mortgage rates would be sub-7% if spreads return to that level. Historically, mortgage spreads have ranged from 1.60% to 1.80%. Last week, spreads rose to 2.27% from 2.23% a week earlier. Let’s compare last week’s mortgage rates to where they would have been at the best spread levels this year and the worst levels of this cycle. If we had the best levels of spreads in 2026, mortgage rates would be 6.72% today, not 7.17% . If we had the worst mortgage spread levels of 2023, mortgage rates would be 8.11% today, not 7.17% . Weekly pending sales Our pending home sales data provides a week-to-week perspective, though holidays and short-term fluctuations can affect results. This weekly pending sales data typically takes 30-60 days to reflect in sales data. The key for the last three weeks: lower rates, even above 7%, have stabilized demand, as our weekly pending sales have shown. Now, this isn’t growth, just stabilization from a noticeable slowdown when mortgage rates got toward 7.60%. The last three years and 10 months show that housing demand grows when mortgage rates fall below 6.64% and head toward 6%; above 7%, we don’t have much growth data beyond seasonal demand. Last year at this time, mortgage rates were headed toward 6%, so the year-over-year comps will be hard for some time. Here are the pending sales for last week over the last two years: 2026: 51,764 2025: 59,164 Purchase applications Purchase application data, which looks out 30-90 days, has softened as mortgage rates rose above 6.64% and are now above 7%. We had a small decline week to week; I can see the stabilization here as well and the year-over-year comps will also be very difficult here, as last year at this time rates were heading toward 6%. Earlier in the year, when rates were lower, pretty much every week this year showed growth. Here are the stats on purchase apps so far in 2026: 16 positive week-to-week prints 24 negative week-to-week prints 5 flat week-to-week prints 10 weeks of double-digit year-over-year growth 25 weeks of positive year-over-year growth 15 negative year-over-year prints Housing inventory Housing inventory growth has been very tame this year, with some weeks being down year over year. However, when mortgage rates got above 6.64% and then headed toward 7.60%, we did see some growth pick up. Also, rates were lower last year so demand was heading toward a nine-month high in December, which means it the comps will be easier to show growth in inventory. Inventory growth is running at 7.18% even with easier comps. Weekly inventory change (Oct. 30-Nov. 6): Inventory fell from 914,833 to 902,740 Same week last year (Oct. 31-Nov 7): Inventory fell from 856,751 to 842,257 New listings New listings are in their typical seasonal decline; 2026 has been the healthiest new-listings year since 2022, with over 80,000 new listings per week a few times this year. The concern I had was that if higher rates cause sellers to stop listing their homes — as they did in the second half of 2022 — that would hurt supply and demand. However, that hasn’t happened in any meaningful way. Most home sellers are buyers, and now that rates have fallen a smidge, it looks like we can end the year on a positive note for 2026 for new listings. In a normal environment, new listings range from 80,000 to 100,000 per week during peak periods. For context, during the housing bubble years, new listings ranged from 250,000 to 400,000 per week for several years . Here is last week’s new listings data for the past two years: 2026: 54,479 2025: 55,486 Price-cut percentage Typically, about one-third of homes see price reductions before they sell, reflecting the housing market’s dynamic nature. Overall, price-cut percentages this year have been lower than last year. This held true until rates moved above 6.64% and then above 7%; demand fell, and the year-over-year price-cut percentage rose 1%. items.title: Why didn’t the strong jobs report send mortgage rates skyrocketing?
items.description: With all the crazy things happening this week, the blowout jobs report on Friday didn’t send mortgage rates up at all. But one thing is for sure: the labor market has been better in 2026 than it was in 2025. I once labelled the labor market the honey badger labor market and no matter what has been thrown at the U.S. economy after 2011 — outside the brief recession created by COVID-19 — the labor data has held up well. Let’s dig into why very strong jobs report didn’t push yields or mortgage rates higher, as we would normally expect with the Fed being so hawkish in their statement. From BLS : Total nonfarm payroll employment rose by 165,000 in October, and the unemployment rate changed little at 4.1 percent, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today. Employment increased in professional and business services, in health care, and in transportation and warehousing. The labor data has improved enough that we have gone from a 4.5% unemployment rate last year to 4.1% today. Part of this is that labor-force growth has slowed and the break-even number has decreased, meaning fewer jobs are needed to keep the unemployment rate low. I have my break-even at 78,000 jobs created per month; I believe the Fed's is 33,000. Some economists have it at zero, which I think is silly. In any case, the unemployment rate is lower this year versus last year. Now, the low point in the COVID-19 recovery was about 3.4% unemployment back in 2023, so the unemployment rate has increased from that low, but it's still good enough to keep the Fed’s focus on inflation instead of labor. Jobs breakdown This month's report had growth in a few sectors, especially the business services sector jobs with one of the biggest monthly prints in years. There was also growth in manufacturing, and transportation & warehouse, while construction jobs faded a tad. Construction labor will be interesting in the future if mortgage rates stay elevated and short-term rates go up. If there is an AI slowdown and fewer AI data centers are being built, will this sector start to decline? One of my most critical recession indicators, residential construction employment, doesn’t look great lately, but it isn’t looking terrible either. In previous cycles, you can see a clear downtrend in this labor pool, which hasn’t happened in this cycle. With builders doing more rate buydowns — which have kept new home sales at 2019 levels over the past few years — and remodeling work holding up, this clear recession indicator hasn’t broken yet. 10-year yield and mortgage rates As crazy as this week has been, the jobs data wasn’t the big driver of mortgage rates as much as AI stock prices. CoreWeave's stock price was up 10% pre-market today, and bond yields ticked up with that. The jobs report didn’t do much to yields, we just saw a mild increase and then they fell back in line with the trend. Then CoreWeave stock price went almost negative, bond yields fell to the lows of the day, and now both have picked up from the lows! The market needs a weekend break. Mortgage rates ended the day flat at 7.17%, so as crazy as this sounds, the blowout jobs data didn’t send mortgage rates or bond yields much higher. That's good news for rates, and there are some levers the new Congress can pull to potentially get rates even lower, which I discussed on today's episode of the HousingWire Daily podcast with Editor in Chief Sarah Wheeler. Conclusion A lot has changed this week for the economy regarding the bond market and where mortgage rates can go. The blue wave has raised hopes that the trade war and the conflict with Iran can end soon, AI companies have shown they can bleed, and Congress will try to slow the AI boom as much as it can without crashing it. All these things happened this week, so that even with four solid jobs reports during jobs week, the 10-year yield closed at 4.86% and mortgage rates closed at weekly lows. Related More: Jobs Report

items.title: Opendoor says it's behind schedule but plans to catch up by 2027
items.description: Opendoor is behind schedule. Since taking over the company a little over a year ago, CEO Kaz Nejatian has promised that the firm would achieve adjusted net income positive status on a 12-month go-forward basis by the end of 2026. But the recent housing market downturn, triggered by the rapid rise in mortgage rates , has proven to be a bit of a roadblock. “We are currently behind but we intend to catch up,” the iBuyer’s third quarter 2026 earnings report explained. During the quarter, Opendoor recorded an adjusted net loss of $66 million and an actual net loss of $218 million, up from a $90 million net loss a year ago. This comes even as the company reported a 12% annual increase in revenue to $1.022 billion. “A year ago, I told you we would build a different Opendoor — faster, stronger, fully committed to our mission of tilting the world in favor of homeowners,” Nejatian said during his firm’s earnings call with investors and analysts on Thursday. “We have spent the past year building a machine, and that machine is getting better every single day. We are not done yet. It is not perfect, but it is getting better every single day. The question is this: Is Opendoor in a better economic condition than it was a year ago? The answer is obviously yes.” A more resilient Opendoor Nejatian’s confidence comes from his belief that Opendoor has become more resilient over the past year. This includes ways in which the company has worked to serve more sellers without adding more homes to the company’s balance sheet. “This past week, around half of the first offers our direct-to-consumer sellers accepted were listing or Cash Now, More Later. That lets us serve more sellers with less of our capital exposed to changes in the market,” Nejatian said. In the past 12 months, the company has done over $1 billion in Cash Now, More Later volume. “We have built more ways to meet sellers' needs and have made it easier for them to understand their options and make the choice they want for their own lives,” Nejatian said. “Sellers can now adjust the offer slides and make the choice that is good for their families.” Scaling without buying more homes? Nejatian noted that every other time Opendoor has tried to scale, it has done so by purchasing more properties, but that isn’t the case this time. “We proved that we can grow without buying growth. That's the single most important thing that has happened over the last year. We're changing that with our capital-light products,” Nejatian said. Still, Opendoor did purchase far more homes in Q3 2026 than it did in Q3 2025, with a 316% year-over-year increase to 4,865 homes. The company’s signed acquisition volume represented an estimated 0.56% of market share in the addressable U.S. market in Q3 2026 — more than four times higher than a year ago. On the sales side, Opendoor sold 2,728 homes, an increase of 160 homes compared to a year ago. At the end of the quarter, the iBuyer had 7,596 homes in its inventory, up from 3,139 homes a year ago. While the increase in inventory could be seen as cause for concern, especially heading into the slower winter housing market, Opendoor noted that homes listed for sale for 120 days represented just 18% of inventory at the end of the quarter, down from 50% a year ago. Despite the progress, Nejatian said the company still has work left to do on unit economics and resale velocity, something it needs to focus on as it strives for more resiliency. “We're not as good as we want to be, but we're in a much better place," he said. "When the market moves against you and you own homes, there's two things you can do. You can sell fast, or you can hold and wait and pray for the market to recover. We choose to clear. "The decline in late August and September knocked us off track on execution a little bit because we turned our attention to clearance rather than margin improvement. It costs something real in a quarter like this, but that's the right way to run this company for the long run.” To help with some of these challenges, Nejatian said Opendoor has turned to AI to help improve speed while still scaling. Some of these tools include an AI model that determines repair plans for every home to hit the market. The company said the system has been outperforming the old process of following a standard repair manual. Opendoor said it also built a system to help price homes. While humans still have final judgment, the software does the work of pulling applicable, comparable homes. Ancillary services and the future Nejatian also said that Opendoor is focusing on its mortgage division . In Q3, Opendoor said originations from its in-house lender were up 400% year over year. This comes as the iBuyer's lender is now licensed in 25 states, compared to none a year ago. In addition, the company also launched a beta test of Buy with Opendoor in the San Francisco Bay Area this week. The product allows the company to earn mortgage revenue on properties not affiliated with Opendoor in anyway. Looking to the future, Nejatian said Opendoor is hoping to build out title and escrow services — not only to add more efficiencies to Opendoor’s in-house transactions but to add additional revenue streams by serving consumers not in its ecosystem. “We need to grow, use less capital per transaction, and sell homes faster. Those are things we can control, and that is what we are focused on. What matters to us is solving the core problems of our business, and those are what we need to focus on,” Nejatian said. items.title: Progress Residential to pay $49.8M to settle FTC, state claims over rental practices
items.description: Progress Residential , the property manager of single-family rental homes owned by Pretium Partners , has agreed to pay $49.8 million to settle deceptive and unfair practices claims by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and state regulators. The company denies any wrongdoing. In a complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia , regulators alleged that the company advertised rental prices that did not reflect the full amount tenants would be required to pay, imposed hidden or inadequately disclosed fees and charges, and mishandled security deposits. The claims also included that Progress misrepresented the condition and move-in readiness of properties, restricted tenants’ ability to share reviews, and failed to adequately address tenant complaints and maintenance issues. In a statement given to HousingWire , a representative of Progress Residential and Pretium said the companies have reached an agreement “with the FTC and four states to resolve the Commission’s Civil Investigative Demand related to certain aspects of our resident experience during the period of 2021 to 2025.” “The agreement contains no admission of wrongdoing, and we maintain Progress’ practices have been transparent, fair, and consistent with industry practice,” the spokesperson said. “Although we disagree with the FTC’s claims, this resolution allows us to move forward with our mission of expanding access to quality, affordable rental housing in neighborhoods of opportunity.” The deal was reached by the FTC, the attorneys general of Arizona, Indiana and Colorado, and the Utah Division of Consumer Protection . It combines monetary relief for renters across the country. “We will always welcome investment in housing and recognize the important role private capital can play in increasing opportunities for Hoosier families,” Indiana Attorney General Todd Rokita said in a statement. “But no company, regardless of size or financial backing, gets a free pass to mislead consumers, impose hidden charges or treat tenants unfairly.” “Consumers searching for housing should have access to straightforward information about the costs associated with renting a home,” said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection. “Transparency regarding rental prices and fees helps consumers compare options and make informed choices. Clear pricing practices also support competition by allowing housing providers to compete on the basis of price, quality and service. "The FTC is monitoring the rental housing market and will continue to take action where appropriate to ensure that consumers receive clear and accurate information about the costs of renting a home.” Per the settlement terms, Progress must disclose the total monthly rental price in advertisements and listings, along with mandatory fees and charges, before a consumer commits to rent. The company also must stop withholding funds for ordinary wear and tear and is prohibited from misleading claims about property conditions. The consumer redress funds created by the settlement total $48.5 million and will be used for relief as directed by the stipulated order entered in the federal case. Arizona is receiving $1.25 million. In 2024, Invitation Homes , the largest owner of U.S. single-family rental homes, agreed to pay $48 million to consumers and change some of its practices. items.title: 220-Unit Mixed-Use Project Moves Forward Near Rowan University
items.description: Hundreds of new apartments have been approved on a former industrial site in the center of a South Jersey college town. Google Maps 220 Rowan Blvd., another Nexus Properties project in Glassboro The Glassboro Planning Board voted Wednesday to greenlight Nexus Properties ’ plans for 220 units and about 8K SF of retail on the corner of Academy and East High streets in the town's central business district, 42Freeway reported . The market-rate project, dubbed Glassworks, will span two city blocks and six stories on a site about three-quarters of a mile from the core of Rowan University’s campus. Nexus expects the project to deliver sometime in 2029, 70and73 reported . Its new retail component will effectively be a replacement for older commercial properties that existed on the site. The site once housed the Whitney Glass Works, which closed in the 1920s. The Heritage Glass Museum operates in the neighborhood and will remain open, alongside Angelo’s Diner. The former Glassboro Library is set to be razed. Lawrenceville-based Nexus is also a major student housing owner in Glassboro, with five properties listed on its website. Some of those are part of the Rowan Boulevard project, where Nexus struck up a $425M public-private partnership with Rowan University to build a mixed-use neighborhood overlooking the campus. While permitting can be a challenge in South Jersey, the region is seeing some multifamily development, a large share of which is affordable housing meant to meet state requirements for municipalities under the Mount Laurel doctrine. Enforcement of the 1975 New Jersey Supreme Court decision requiring local governments to use zoning to further attainable housing production was clarified in 2024. That push is also underway in Voorhees, where 180 affordable units are on the way. Administrators there greenlit plans for a 178-unit, market-rate office-to-residential conversion last month. But mixed-use plans for a redevelopment of the nearby Echelon Mall have fallen through since they were introduced last year, the Philadelphia Business Journal reported this week. Hoboken Brownstone Co . told the outlet this was due to uncertainty about a $90M tax credit it sought through New Jersey’s Aspire program, which has paused its application process. items.title: NYC Claims Nearly Half Of State's Opportunity Zones, Putting New Neighborhoods In Play
items.description: The opportunity zone guessing game is over. On Thursday, the Treasury Department released the official list of census tracts eligible for the federal tax incentive program's second iteration, giving investors sitting in Park Avenue towers a new map to pore over. Pexels/Raphael Loquellano Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant is among the neighborhoods designated as opportunity zones. “About $100B was deployed in the last decade to the program, probably half of that was quote-unquote institutional capital,” Ackman-Ziff Real Estate Group Director Andrew Rudy said. “I wouldn't be surprised if there was a doubling of capital formation for this iteration of the law versus the last.” Leading up to the release, New York was among the few states to publicize little information about the process. Stricter requirements for census tracts qualifying as “economically distressed” and Congress’ aim of funneling more money toward rural areas raised concerns over which New York City neighborhoods would be selected. The final deadline for states to submit their opportunity zone nominations was Oct. 28, after which Treasury reviewed them before releasing the full list. New York ultimately had 430 census tracts designated as opportunity zones, 210 of which are in the five boroughs. Brooklyn and the Bronx received the greatest number of designations, with 67 and 57, respectively. Another 41 are in Manhattan , 35 are in Queens and 10 are on Staten Island . The program allows investors to defer capital gains taxes and lower the basis on which they are taxed by investing in real estate projects or businesses that spur economic growth in select low-income communities. OZ 1.0, created under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 , used 2010 census data, allowing several neighborhoods already booming with development to qualify. It also gave benefits to projects in tracts adjacent to qualifying zones — a loophole that was removed from 2.0 — further drawing investment to highly developed neighborhoods. Because OZ 2.0 is based on the 2020 census, many areas that benefited the most under the program’s predecessor no longer qualify. Still, New York City’s density, alongside public housing developments and rent-stabilized units, means that some neighborhoods that don’t seem blighted qualify under the poverty threshold. The new map includes parts of Manhattan’s Lower East Side , Harlem and the Upper West Side , but the more appealing sites may be in areas where developers can layer subsidies, according to Ackman-Ziff Director Jordan Brustein. “For example, Yonkers , which is a more emerging area, is still well located on the transportation line and near the city. Developers are able to get unique incentives that yield better returns, which ultimately end up attracting more equity,” Brustein said. “So to us, we're more interested there than maybe even some of these better-located assets that have thinner return profiles.” Prized areas of the outer boroughs include Brooklyn’s Bedford-Stuyvesant , which has become increasingly gentrified, and areas of the East Bronx near the Metro-North’s station expansion. Queens’ Sunnyside Yards , where Mayor Zohran Mamdani is seeking to advance a 12,000-unit residential development , also received designation, despite not being on the initial list of eligible tracts. It is only one of two tracts nationwide to do so, with the other being in Hawaii. But unlike rural areas of the country, where the primary issue for development is attracting capital interest, New York City developers struggle with policies that make building more difficult. Under 485-x , higher construction wage requirements kick in for larger housing projects. As a result, the vast majority of proposals filed in the last two years are for buildings with 99 units or less. Rudy and Brustein said many investors are gravitating toward shovel-ready sites eligible under 1.0 as they raise capital for 2.0. Despite stronger markets like Long Island City no longer being included, the two-year transition period allows developers to continue accepting funds. Faced with higher interest rates and stricter lending standards , some developers in OZ 1.0 zones have pushed through the predevelopment process only to stall out before getting shovels in the ground. As long as they’ve followed compliance, those projects are likely to be among the first to be injected with OZ 2.0 funds. “Think about it this way: There’s a reason why they’re not in 2.0 maps,” Brustein said. “The capital markets have been challenging, and the one bright spot right now in the market is opportunity zones .” Continue reading this story with a free account Log in or register Related Topics: Ackman-Ziff Real Estate Group , Brooklyn , Manhattan , Opportunity zones , opportunity zones 2.0 , Queens , Staten Island , Sunnyside Yards , The Bronx

items.description: GSE delinquencies climb: Don't shift staff solely to FHA By Spencer Lee CloseText About Spencer twitter Spencer_NYC linkedin spencer-lee-journo Published November 06, 2026, 4:11 p.m. EST | Updated November 06, 2026, 5:21 p.m. EST 2 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email What's at Stake: Whether mortgage servicers can maintain enough resources to handle rising agency loan distress Supporting Data: 6.9%: The late-summer increase in short-term delinquent GSE-backed mortgages. Overview bullets generated by AI with editorial review. A late-summer rise in delinquencies among mortgages backed by the government-sponsored enterprises points to an upward trend that may require servicers to keep resources available for agency loans until economic conditions improve. Processing Content Delinquency totals increased on a month-to-month basis across stages in August, according to data provided by the Federal Housing Finance Agency, the overseer of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The number of borrowers 30 to 59 days delinquent climbed 6.9% to 313,254 from 292,965 between July and August . The number of mortgages past due by 60 days or more grew 2.9% to 256,999 units compared to 249,816 one month earlier. The representative share of delinquencies relative to all outstanding GSE-backed mortgages now stands at 1.03% for early-stage distress. Liens 60 to 90 days past due make up 0.84% of outstanding mortgages. Borrowers in serious delinquency or currently in foreclosure account for 0.6%. Although mortgage leaders in 2026 raised regular warnings about looming challenges for borrowers with Federal Housing Administration mortgages , the new data hints at difficulties surfacing in the agency segment. While distress eased in the early summer, delinquency volumes finished August higher than where they stood at the end of the first quarter, when they settled at 281,098 and 246,081, respectively. FHFA's findings suggest rising prices and economic uncertainty continue to take a significant toll on the ability of some homeowners to consistently meet monthly mortgage obligations, with downward pressure on affordability becoming more acute as 2026 progresses. The surge in summer delinquencies came at the same time prices of consumer goods ticked upward, with energy costs, in particular, accelerating from the impact of the Iran War. Meanwhile, the still-rising costs of property insurance and taxes are leading to prolonged sticker shock, even as the pace appears to be leveling off this year. Recent forecasts predict many of the same factors will weigh on affordability through next year. The extent of homeowner concerns showed up in the number of calls for legal assistance to deal with potential foreclosures in the late summer, which came in almost 15% higher at the end of the third quarter compared to a year ago. Lawyers at LegalShield specifically noted inflation's effect on household budgets as a primary cause , rather than poor planning on the part of borrowers. Foreclosure starts leap 18% FHFA's new report also found foreclosures on the rise among Fannie Mae- and Freddie Mac-backed loans. The number of foreclosure starts shot up 18% to 8,930 from 7,569 from July to August. Foreclosure and bank sales of properties eased 5%, though, to 1,333 from 1,403. A report from Auction.com saw such inventory likely to increase for the remainder of 2026, but much of the growth will be driven by FHA foreclosures. The FHFA also recorded 7,675 permanent loan modifications in August, increasing from 7,503 a month earlier. More than one-third, or 36.5%, of modifications involved extending the term of payment. In total, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac completed 16,335 actions in August aimed at foreclosure prevention. items.title: Lenders turn to cuts, AI as strong jobs point to rate hikes
items.description: Lenders turn to cuts, AI as strong jobs point to rate hikes By Bonnie Sinnock CloseText About Bonnie twitter bcynic mailto bonnie.sinnock@arizent.com linkedin bonnie-sinnock-115a829 Published November 06, 2026, 1:38 p.m. EST | Updated November 06, 2026, 3:35 p.m. EST 3 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Key Insight: Discover why nonbank mortgage payrolls hit a 2026 low despite rising retail productivity gains. Expert Quote: "For housing, stronger hiring cuts both ways." — Sam Williamson, Senior Economist, First American. Overview bullets generated by AI with editorial review. Nonbank mortgage payroll estimates dropped to a low for 2026 ahead of broader employment gains last month, pointing to a persistent need to manage origination staffing with retail productivity initiatives that have not yet reduced costs but at least contained them. Processing Content Industry-specific data the Bureau of Labor Statistics released with a one-month lag for real-estate credit and loan brokers, when combined, show industry payrolls dropped to 265,100 in August, marking the lowest point since the seasonally-slow first quarter. The statistics, combined with October's strong jobs report signaling a likelihood rates won't immediately fall further , suggest the industry is reducing origination staffing but are able to do so gradually as artificial intelligence has helped boost the number of loans closers handle. "There are a lot of learnings that can happen in this tighter market,'" Walter Mullen, chief strategy officer at Onity , said at IMN's mortgage servicing rights conference this week, noting that origination declines have forced companies to broadly explore operational innovation. Where retail fulfillment productivity stands The number of loans handled by full-time equivalent employees in retail fulfillment have inched up this year primarily due to a surge in closer gains, according to data the Mortgage Bankers Association and Stratmor Group have collected from lenders. The average monthly number of loans per closer jumped from 36.7 to 41.5 between 2025 and 2026 while lenders reported a far more modest gain for processors and a slight decline in productivity in underwriting in line with the more challenging origination environment. Lenders reported a mix of artificial intelligence and leaner staffing drove the productivity gains, which did not reduce costs but have prevented them from rising. Current employment trends: A mixed blessing While the latest industry-specific and total job numbers point to some challenges for mortgage companies, housing economists noted they do point to some offsetting positives for lenders too. "For housing, stronger hiring cuts both ways. More jobs mean more income and more reasons to move, while a stronger economy could prolong the wait for mortgage-rate relief," Sam Williamson, senior economist at First American, wrote in an emailed press statement. October's stronger-than-anticipated gain of 165,000 and a decline in the unemployment rate from 4.2% to 4.1% came with wage gains, according to Williamson. However, MBA noted that there also were indications in the numbers that some workers are underemployed. "While the headline unemployment rate decreased, some of this was due to individuals taking part-time work when they would have preferred a full-time position," MBA Chief Economist Mike Fratantoni wrote in his emailed statement. Despite some signs of weakness like this, Frantantoni said he still anticipates that the overall impact of the numbers will be an increased likelihood that the Federal Open Market Committee will raise short-term rates at one of two of its next meetings. "A resilient job market, combined with inflation that is still too high, is likely to lead the FOMC to hike rates in December. MBA anticipates another hike as well in the first quarter of 2027," he said. While the short-term rates the Fed controls have some bearing on long-term mortgage rates that currently dominate the housing market, mortgage spreads also drive the cost of funds for homebuyers. items.title: Zillow's agent tie-ins grab purchase share as market shrinks
items.description: Zillow's agent tie-ins grab purchase share as market shrinks By Brad Finkelstein CloseText About Brad twitter nmnbrad mailto bradley.finkelstein@arizent.com linkedin brad-finkelstein-8b2b9a5/ Published November 05, 2026, 4:39 p.m. EST | Updated November 05, 2026, 4:45 p.m. EST 3 Min Read Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Zillow's strategy of pairing its loan officers with invitation-only real estate agents is pulling purchase business away from the rest of the market. Its home loans unit grew purchase volume 55% in the third quarter while industry purchase originations fell. Processing Content Zillow Home Loans originated $1.972 billion of purchase loans in the third quarter, up from $1.276 billion a year earlier. Year-to-date volume is up 79%. Over the same quarter, Zillow estimates industry purchase origination volume declined 4%. "It's why purchase mortgage revenue for us is outgrowing the category even with the category declining," said CEO Jeremy Wacksman on the earnings call. The company is almost entirely a purchase lender. It did just $4 million of refinance production in the third quarter, versus $5 million one year prior. Second quarter volume was $2.181 billion, with only $7 million coming from refi. How the Preferred program feeds Zillow Home Loans The volume growth came as Zillow expanded the share of buyer connections sent through its Preferred program, an invitation-only network of real estate agents. Zillow previously called the program Flex. Executives reported double-digit adoption of Zillow Home Loans among customers working with Preferred agents. In Zillow's oldest markets, that rate is approximately 20%. "We are pleased that we continue to see double-digit customer adoption rates in Zillow Home Loans with our oldest markets at approximately 20% adoption rates, demonstrating that our integrated experience is adding value for both consumers and real estate agents," said Jeremy Hoffman, chief operating and chief financial officer. Wacksman framed the integrated model as the reason for Zillow's confidence in mortgage growth. "I mean 80% of buyers need both the mortgage and the agent. They want that as a one-stop shop," he said. "When we can offer that as an integrated experience, that's what they're choosing." He added that "a key part of this strategy is making sure that the Home Loans loan officer and the Preferred agent build a mutually beneficial relationship." The shift also changes how Zillow gets paid. Under its legacy advertising model, real estate agents used co-marketing dollars from lenders when bidding on leads, said Douglas Harter of BTIG. Under the Preferred model, Zillow captures mortgage revenue at origination, which can come six to 12 months later. Why mortgage revenue still missed The volume gains did not translate into the revenue analysts expected. Mortgage revenue rose 32% year-over-year to $70 million, but Keefe, Bruyette & Woods had forecast $81.3 million, putting the result 13.9% short. BTIG had forecast $81 million. Hoffman attributed the miss to " rate shock , which caused lower conversions." Industry purchase volume also came in weaker than Zillow planned for. "We estimate that industry mortgage purchase origination volumes were down 4% for Q3, below our expectation for a low-single-digit decline," he said. "We call out mortgage industry performance because the majority of Zillow buyers purchased their home with a mortgage." Harter tied the broader earnings miss to a weakening housing market and the "accelerated transition from the legacy ad model to Flex." Zillow underperformed existing home sales for the first time since the fourth quarter of 2024, which helped spread the miss into mortgage, he said in a research note. Zillow posted a $158 million net loss for the quarter, compared with $10 million of net income in the third quarter of 2025. Zillow expects a steeper purchase decline in Q4 Zillow guided fourth quarter mortgage revenue to between $55 million and $56 million, with total revenue between $635 million and $665 million. "Our revenue outlook includes our expectation for a decline in year-over-year mortgage industry purchase origination volumes of 10% to 15%," Hoffman said. "This is down significantly from our prior industry expectation of mid-single-digits decline due to the sharp increase in mortgage rates we saw at the end of Q3 and into the start of Q4." Zillow expects 20% revenue growth in the fourth quarter as it scales outside its residential business, "with mortgage tailing off," Harter said. "The weakening housing market and bigger-than-anticipated model transition impact contributed to an 8-9% reduction in the 4Q revenue guide from the prior implied level," he said. "Headwinds are expected to carry into '27." Brad Finkelstein Originations Editor Brad Finkelstein is the originations editor of National Mortgage News. items.title: Two Neighboring $9.9 Million Oceanfront Homes Just Listed in Kauai’s South Shore—And They Can Form an Ultra-Luxe Compound
items.description: Tucked into a private-club community in Hawaii called Kukui‘ula , two luxury homes just hit the market on Kauai's South Shore . Set right on the ocean, and set among lush tropical vegetation, this walkable community is only 25-minute drive from Lihue Airport. "The close proximity of everything is very convenient. You’re not having to spend a lot of time in the car,” says Pancho Sullivan of Hawaii Life , who is co-listing the two homes with Haunani Sullivan as well as Suzanne Harding and Jeff Skinner of Kukui‘ula Realty Group . The asking price sits at $9,900,000 each. Both were built in 2025 and have never been occupied. Aepo Nei 18 and Aepo Nei 19 are neighboring 3,372-square-foot homes with four bedrooms and 4.5 baths each. They can be purchased together, to create a private compound, or by separate buyers. Even better, the homes are fully furnished and stocked with items like bed and bath linens, beach towels, and everything you need to cook and serve in the kitchen, such as bowls, plates and glasses. Loading... Aepo Nei 18’s layout features connected pavilions. Steven Lippman / homesbystevenlippman.com Loading... The homes both feature 180-degree ocean views. Steven Lippman / homesbystevenlippman.com Loading... The homes feature lush living areas. Loading... The homes were constructed with natural materials like lava stone, coral and teak. Steven Lippman / homesbystevenlippman.com But it’s the design by Brazil-based Architects+CO that’s truly unique. Kauai Bahia Construction and their in-house material company, Kayu, handled all of the finish material production and millwork installation. "Brazil is known for incredible resort-club communities," says Pancho. "We actually traveled to Brazil to look at some of the clubs they designed. It’s the same tropical feel (as Hawaii) that blends in really well with nature." Aepo Nei 18’s layout features connected pavilions while Aepo Nei 19’s living spaces open onto a lawn courtyard. Design features at both include deep roof overhangs, walls of glass and multiple outdoor living spaces such as an infinity-edge pool; jacuzzi; swim-in, swim-out sauna; and in-water fire pit. "They both have beautiful 180-degree ocean views looking across the Tom Weiskopf -designed golf course. The swim-in, swim-out dry sauna facing the ocean is a unique feature," says Pancho, adding that the usage of natural materials like lava stone, coral and teak "fit into the landscape very beautifully." Referred to as the Garden Island, Kauai is home to about 73,000 people. "We get the majority of the island’s sunshine down here," says Haunani, about the South Shore. "People flock here for the beaches and the sunshine, Hawaiian monk seals on the sand, and a lot of ocean activity including surfing. "A lot of people that venture to Kauai are adventure seekers. We have great hiking. You can get on a boat and dive on the Nā Pali Coast and do ziplining and ATV tours." Loading... The exterior Aepo Nei 19’, which features deep roof overhangs. Steven Lippman / homesbystevenlippman.com Loading... One of the bathrooms, with natural features. Loading... Both homes come fully furnished. Stand-up paddleboarding, diving and fishing are two other activities easy to do in this community. Homeowners become club members with access to dining, a pool, spa (boasting a steam rook and lava-rock dry sauna), pickleball and tennis courts, and an 18-hole golf course. "There’s an incredible gym with classes daily, from yoga to sound bathing to fitness training," says Pancho. "All of that is part of your club membership. It’s a great place to be in tune with nature and get healthy." A 10-acre organic garden features a farm stand as well as opportunities to create floral bouquets. There’s also a conscious effort to honor Hawaiian history through cultural-heritage walks; sunrise ceremonies; hula performances; and classes in Hawaiian featherwork, quilting and basket weaving. “Members who are part of the club become life-long friends,” says Haunani. “They’re going to each other’s second homes and weddings. They travel around the world together.” The community also organizes annual golf and pickleball tournaments for members, and three golf courses are within a seven-minute drive. Loading... Like it's neighbor, the home features 180-degree ocean views. Loading... The living areas open onto an open courtyard and pool area. Another incentive is that the community’s zoned as a Vacation Destination Area. This means properties can join the short-term rental pool, for minimum seven-night stays. "Some of the owners put their homes in the rental pool and block out time for themselves and their families. That’s a great added benefit," says Haunani, as few club communities on Kauai allow this. The Sullivans think the buyer will likely hail from the West Coast, enticed by a direct flight from hubs in cities like Los Angeles, San Francisco, Seattle, Phoenix and Denver that arrive on the island by mid-day. “Kukui‘ula is a great place for families to gather and spend time together. We see a lot of members bring their entire families so they can vacation together multiple times per year,” says Pancho. “With all these activities it’s easy to curate an incredible vacation with the convenience of being on property. items.title: Meet the 27-Year-Old Who’s Trying To Bring Housing Back to Rural Ohio
items.description: When it comes to the hottest locations that attract young 20-somethings, Mansfield, OH , probably isn't the first place that comes to mind. For years, Mansfield’s nickname was “The Fun Center of Ohio ” because of its family-friendly attractions and its status in the 1970s as a mini-bike manufacturing hub. More recently, the town of 47,000, located halfway between Columbus and Cleveland , earned the local nickname of “Danger City” after the Westinghouse electric plant left in 1990 and the town fell into deep economic decline. That didn’t stop Ben Goehner . The 27-year-old serial entrepreneur, who started a painting and landscaping business as a teenager, relocated to Mansfield from Seattle a year ago, hoping to revitalize rural housing through his vertically integrated housing development company, Western Dominion Land . Vertical integration is a development model in which a single company controls the full life cycle of a housing project. “In other countries, they’ve figured out that vertically integrating construction means you’re not paying a margin out to every single step," Goehner explains. "If you own the system—from a lumberyard, to producing panels or modular, to buying the land, to developing the land, to building the homes—you're not paying everyone’s markup along the way, and you can actually deliver that home at a reasonable price.” Goehner is building a factory in Mansfield to produce structured panels that he says will cut single-family home construction from months to weeks and allow him to charge much less than other builders. The first panels are expected to roll off the production line in early 2027. Currently, it takes 8.8 months to construct a home from start to finish, according to the National Association of Home Builders . Goehner says his process allows a home to be built and move-in-ready in 40 days. Western Dominion has already built about 500 housing units across Ohio, starting at $200,000 for a single-family home. Western Dominion focuses on what it calls "attainable housing"—homes priced below what the median household income in the area can afford but not income-limited, meaning they work for the vast majority of families and buyers. In Mansfield, where the median listing price is $229,000, he says, "single-family homes at $215,000 sold instantly. At $260,000, they sat for months." Loading... Ben Goehner says rural housing development has been sorely overlooked by large-scale developers. Ben Goehner As he sees it, 25% of the homes on the market are priced for 60% to 70% of buyers, while the rest of what’s being built is at the top end of the market. Furthermore, only 8% of construction happens in rural areas, despite 20% of the population living there. "The government is too focused on low-income housing" and low-income housing tax credits, he says. “And the last few housing bills they passed were only structured to deliver essentially more urban multifamily units and incentivize builders to build more low-income housing with tax credits." In rural communities, he adds, “We have a terrible amount of aged housing inventory. Most of our homes are from before 1970, which would be fine if it didn't cost so much to remodel. “From the '90s to the 2000s, we’re building a good amount of homes. As a country, we were doing about 1.6 million a year. And then in rural America, we were doing about 220,000 homes a year. And then 2008 hits, and that drops down to about 60,000 homes a year in rural America." Along the way, smaller builders disappeared, and larger builders were disincentivized from building in rural areas because of the red tape involved. "If you want to build in rural America and you go to a bank, unless you have all the cash, you have to show comps," he says. "You've got to be, like, ‘All right, we think these homes are going to sell for this much because these guys sold for this much.' And if no one's built for five to 50 years, which is the case in a lot of these communities, that can be difficult." The added costs of building in rural areas, like having to pull utilities, "mean you're spending $25,000 to $50,000 per lot before you can even start putting a house on it or connecting your utilities to the lot." Since the COVID-19 pandemic, home prices in rural communities have risen sharply. A Realtor.com® housing analysis of home prices from November 2019 to November 2025 found that median listing prices increased more than 70% in rural counties while in-metro counties saw home prices increase around 30% during the same time period. "A lot of the politicians we talk to, they go, 'I didn't know that that county needed housing. I didn't know rural needed housing because the population is shrinking.' But then when you look at why the population is shrinking, it's because they haven't gotten any new homes for 20 to 40 years." "You've got this huge demand. items.title: Camden lowers guidance after September concession resurgence
items.description: Camden lowers guidance after September concession resurgence The REIT still saw improvement in expenses and new lease growth in Q3, though rising interest rates forced it to cancel property and land acquisitions. Published Nov. 6, 2026 Leslie Shaver Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Wall Street sign with american flags and New York Stock Exchange in Manhattan, New York City, USA. Getty Images Camden’s Property Trust lowered its 2026 same-store revenue midpoint by 50 basis points to 0% after a weaker-than-expected September and the expectation of greater seasonal decline in the fourth quarter, according to the REIT’s executives on Friday’s third-quarter earnings call. Performance in September, specifically, surprised the company and set the stage for that revision, according to CEO Alex Jessett. “It was a greater decline in traffic than we had expected,” Jessett said. “And when we had the decline in traffic, obviously, you have to reduce your prices if you're trying to increase traffic.” Jessett said concessions, which were “incredibly sticky,” ranged from three weeks in West Palm Beach, Florida, up to two months in Austin, Texas, as merchant builders continued to offer steep discounts. “The third quarter, at least July and August, were so strong that we would have expected to see others start to dial back their concessions, and they absolutely did not do it,” Jessett said. Despite the September slowdown, there were positives: Camden expects same-store YOY expense growth of 1.75%, which is 75 bps better than the REIT’s prior midpoint and 125 bps better than beginning-of-year guidance, according to CFO Ben Fraker. The company was also “the only S&P 500 multifamily REIT to experience sequential improvement for both new lease rates and blended lease rates each quarter this year, and we were the only one with second- to third-quarter acceleration,” according to Jessett. Camden saw positive signs into Q4, though high-concession markets weighed on results. The REIT finalized its massive California sale and multiple acquisitions, though the interest rate environment forced it to cancel other deals. Rent trends Like many companies in supply heavy markets, Camden saw new leases remain in negative territory in Q3, falling to -2% YOY, according to its Q3 earnings release. In Q2, Camden’s new lease rate came in 130 bps lower at -3.3%. In Q3, renewals rose 3.6% YOY, giving the REIT a blended rate of 1%. In Q2, renewals increased 2.8% YOY and blends were -0.2%. “While renewal growth was in line with our expectations, new lease and blended lease growth were at the low end of our anticipated ranges, likely driven by the persistent concessions that remain in many of our core markets and sub-markets,” Camden Chief Operating Officer Laurie Baker said on the Q3 call. Camden sent out renewal offers to residents with December and January expirations at an average increase of 4.5%, according to Baker. That isn’t the only positive indicator. “We have seen signed new leases improve pretty dramatically in October as compared to September, and when we look at our October numbers and we compare them to October of last year, we're seeing really significant improvement,” Jessett said. Southeast Florida, at 1.6% YOY revenue growth; Atlanta, at 1.5%; Dallas, at 0.8%; and Houston, at 0.6%, were the top markets for Camden in Q3, according to a company Securities & Exchange Commission filing. Concessions have played a role in their performance, according to Baker. “We're seeing the strongest markets in Atlanta, Southeast Florida, Dallas and Houston,” Baker said. “And so, where those lower concessions are, we're obviously getting a little more pricing power, and we're having the ability to improve our occupancy.” On the other end of the spectrum were Denver, with a 5% YOY revenue decline; Nashville at -3.1%; Tampa, Florida, at -1.3%; and Orlando, Florida, at -0.7%, according to the SEC filing. “We still are continuing to see Denver and Nashville as those that have concessions that have been persistent,” Baker said. Buying and selling In July, Camden closed its sale of 11 properties with 3,620 apartment homes to a BlackRock-managed vehicle for $1.6 billion, recognizing a gain of $1 billion. The REIT used approximately $0.9 billion to retire balances outstanding under its unsecured revolving credit facility and commercial paper program, according to the Q3 earnings release. The REIT used $125 million to fund its August property and land acquisitions; $50 million to repurchase shares in August and early September; and $495 million toward the redemption of $500 million of senior notes due in November and to pay down borrowings in its commercial paper program. It had $55 million remaining in cash investment accounts for general corporate purposes, Fraker said on the call. In Q3, the REIT acquired Camden Brandon, a 296-unit property in Tampa; Camden LoSo, a 343-unit property in Charlotte, North Carolina; and Camden Gulch, a 300-unit property in Nashville, Tennessee, for a combined $305.2 million, according to the release. Camden acquired a land parcel in Tampa for approximately $18.3 million and sold 2.6 acres of land in Los Angeles for approximately $10.7 million, according to the release. Camden canceled the purchase of two properties and one land parcel in Q3 after interest rates rose , according to Jessett. “We went back looking for price adjustments, and clearly the sellers were not quite willing to capitulate to what we were looking for,” Jessett said. The REIT has also decided not to move forward with Nashville and Denver development projects at this time. items.title: October 2026 Jobs Report: Employment growth tops market forecasts
items.description: October 2026 Jobs Report: Employment growth tops market forecasts Written by Kenny Lee on November 6, 2026 Key findings U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, while gains in September and August were revised up by a combined 84,000. The unemployment rate slipped to 4.1% from 4.2% as strong employment growth absorbed an increase in labor force participation. Wage growth continued to cool compared to recent years, with average hourly earnings rising 3.1% year over year. What happened: The nonfarm payroll employment rose 165,000 in October, topping financial market expectations. Combined with strong upward revisions to increases in September and August, the Bureau of Labor Statistics report this month indicates a meaningful improvement in job growth. The increases in employment were broad-based across key industries such as professional and business services (+70,000); healthcare and social assistance (+55,000); and transportation and warehousing (+25,000). Employment in temporary help services, a leading indicator for overall labor demand, soared to 18,600. The household survey also indicates a resilient labor market. The labor force participation rate increased to 61.9% from 61.8% as more workers rejoined the workforce. Combined with strong increases in employment, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1% from 4.2%. Why it matters for housing: Stable employment and wage growth give households the confidence to buy a home or sign a new lease, but the housing market is already feeling the chilling effects of the recent surge in mortgage rates. Zillow data points to a colder-than-usual fall market: our preliminary measure of existing home sales fell 8.7% year over year in October. Newly pending listings — a leading indicator of next month’s closed sales — fell 16.8% year over year, the biggest decrease since August 2023. With mortgage rates above 7%, affordability headwinds in the housing market may still feel insurmountable — even for those who have a job or recently found one. This is consistent with our expectation for a more substantial decline in existing home sales and slower growth in home value in Q4. While mortgage rates have been declining from their recent peak, it is difficult to know how far they will fall when forces pushing up Treasury yields, such as anxiety over government deficits and geopolitical impact on energy prices, remain at play. But when mortgage rates come down, eventually, buyers will be ready. The Bureau of Labor Statistics report today is consistent with a stable labor market in a growing economy. The resilient labor market will pave the way for a housing market thaw. Wacker Drive, a premier Class A office tower overlooking the Chicago River in downtown Chicago, to Prime Finance and Hines. Situated along the Chicago River at the intersection of Wacker Drive and Franklin Street, 225 W. Wacker is a 31-story, approximately 651,000-square-foot Class A office tower located where Chicago's West Loop and River North neighborhoods converge. Recognized as one of the city's premier riverfront office assets, the property is home to a diverse roster of leading corporate and professional services firms, including Cushman & Wakefield, which will remain an anchor tenant under the building's new ownership. Cushman & Wakefield is expected to be retained to oversee 225 W. Wacker's property management and agency leasing on behalf of Prime Finance. During Spear Street Capital's tenure, the property underwent significant capital improvements that enhanced the tenant experience and strengthened its position as one of Chicago's most sought-after office destinations. These investments included a transformational lobby renovation, upgraded conferencing and collaboration spaces, a hospitality-driven tenant lounge, state-of-the-art fitness facilities and an expansive outdoor rooftop terrace. "The building's recent transformation, amenity enhancements and leasing momentum generated significant investor interest. Prime Finance and Hines are acquiring a highly differentiated property that is well-positioned for immediate and long-term success in one of the nation's strongest and most resilient office submarkets." The property features direct access to Chicago's Riverwalk and is strategically located near the city's transportation network, restaurants, hotels and entertainment destinations. The new ownership plans additional investments to further elevate the tenant experience, including a re-envisioned lobby-level restaurant and bar that will activate the building's ground floor and enhance its connection to the riverfront. items.description: The U.S. labor market came roaring back in October after September's initial estimated gain of 29,000 new jobs with a reported increase of 165,000 jobs for the month, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Revisions to the August and September numbers boosted previous estimates by a combined 84,000 additional jobs, bringing the year-to-date total through October to 861,000 jobs gained compared to 116,000 total jobs added in all of 2025. items.description: October marked the first month of rent cuts in the U.S. apartment market in 2026, but annual gains continue at a robust pace. items.title: San Diego apartment supply is about to peak
items.description: San Diego apartment supply hit a record high in the past year and is set to peak in 1st quarter 2027. In the year-ending 3rd quarter 2026, roughly 6,600 units completed across San Diego, marking the highest annual total since Realpage Market Analytics began tracking the market in 2000. Supply in the past year also surpassed the market's decade average around the 4,000-unit mark. Annual supply in San Diego is expected to remain elevated, peaking in the year-ending 1st quarter 2027, when roughly 6,880 units are scheduled for completion. items.title: Top 10 Opportunity Zones Where Median Home Prices Nearly Doubled in Q3 2026
items.description: Top 10 Opportunity Zones Where Median Home Prices Nearly Doubled in Q3 2026 by Megan Hunt | Nov 6, 2026 | #figuresfriday , Real Estate News - Recent Articles According to ATTOM’s Q3 2026 Opportunity Zone Report median single-family home and condo prices increased from the second quarter to the third quarter of 2026 in 48.1 percent (1,651) of the 3,431 Opportunity Zone tracts with enough data for both periods. https://www.attomdata.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/ATTOM_Q3_2026_Opportunity_Zones_Top_10.mp4 WATCH ATTOM #figuresfriday: Top 10 Opportunity Zones Where Median Home Price Nearly Doubled Annually in Q3 2026 The report also noted that on an annual basis, prices rose in 48.9 percent (1,598) of the 3,265 tracts with sufficient data in the third quarters of 2025 and 2026. The analysis found that outside Opportunity Zones, typical home prices increased year over year in 51.6 percent (28,212) of the 54,704 census tracts with sufficient data for both third quarters. That made annual price growth slightly more common outside the designated economic development zones than within them. ATTOM’s latest Opportunity Zones Report also noted that the third quarter of 2026 represented the highest median home value since the beginning of the Great Recession in 2008 for 9.4 percent (357) of Opportunity Zone census tracts. In addition, 27.1 percent of the tracts recorded double-digit annual growth in median home values. In this post , we examine the data behind ATTOM’s Q3 2026 Opportunity Zones Report to identify the 10 Opportunity Zones, with third quarter median price points at $200,000 or greater, where median home prices nearly doubled from the third quarter of 2025 to the third quarter of 2026. Nearly half of the Opportunity Zone tracts analyzed posted year-over-year increases, more than one-quarter recorded double-digit growth, and the top 10 tracts highlighted here saw annual gains ranging from 87.5 percent to 99.7 percent.
